messages:
alex: quick check — ran the new quantized t5-small bring-up across g5(16) in us-east, rtx4090 in us-west, and a mixed 4090+g5 pool in eu-west. seeing odd p95 behavior in eu-west when requests route via edge-eu-a. p50s look fine. any idea if kernel selection is flipping on warmup?
priya: can you drop the perf numbers? p50/p95 and throughput at 8/16 concurrent?
alex: baseline: fp16 default kernels. then int8 quant w/ per-channel. numbers from short run (1000 requests each):
- us-east (g5): p50 34ms, p95 82ms, qps 210 @ batch=1
- us-west (4090): p50 28ms, p95 76ms, qps 240 @ batch=1
- eu-west (mixed via edge-eu-a): p50 32ms, p95 210ms, qps 195 @ batch=1
Most of the p95s map to a 2x hop increase through edge-eu-a based on trace IDs.
sam: that p95 in eu looks like kernel fallback during context switch — do we have logs for kernel selection? which build/commit?
alex: running on canary 2026-03-10 (inference-runtime 1.9.2). kernel logs attached in perf-bot dump (see below).
perf-bot: kernel_select events: [173k entries sampled]
- eu-west node-12: fallback to generic-matmul at 2026-03-18T11:04:12Z for 7% of requests
- us-east node-9: generic fallback 0.2%
- us-west node-4: generic fallback 0.1%
joanne: interesting — edge-eu-a routes to a mixed pool with older driver (cuda 12.1 -> fallback). I saw a kernel blacklist for 12.1 in the rollout notes. think the scheduler is sending a subset to older hosts when capacity spikes.
priya: can you reproduce with forced routing to eu-west pool that only has updated drivers? alex, can you run the same run but pin node labels: "driver=13"? also try batch=4 to see batching impact.
alex: launching a pinned job now. command:
```
loadtest --model t5-small-q8 --region eu-west --node-selector "driver=13" --concurrency 16 --batch 1 --requests 2000 --tag edge-probe-0318
```
will also try batch=4 after this completes.
perf-bot: pinned run started 2026-03-18T11:27:02Z
perf-bot: pinned run complete: p50 31ms, p95 78ms, qps 205 @ batch=1
priya: nice — that confirms driver/kernel mismatch on the older hosts. p95 back to normal when not routed through edge-eu-a fallback hosts.
sam: long-term fix: either update driver on eu pool or extend kernel compatibility list. short-term: can we update routing policy to prefer driver=13 for t5-small until we roll drivers? maybe a routing weight tweak. also consider caching KV across pool to avoid kernel cold paths.
joanne: agree. propose two action items: 1) tag older hosts as "avoid-for-quant" in edge routing for 72h; 2) schedule driver roll to 13.0.2 for eu-west nodes next maintenance window. I'll open infra ticket.
alex: done — infra ticket INF-4872 created with the rollout plan and rollback steps. link: https://tickets/internal/INF-4872
priya: one more thought — the int8 quant path increases reliance on optimized matmul kernels, so fallback cost is higher. add a metric alert for kernel_fallback_rate > 1% on any region to catch this earlier.
sam: creating alert. alert id: MON-1219. threshold 1% over 5m, notify #eng-ml and #eng-infra.
perf-bot: alert MON-1219 created
alex: follow-up: after pin + driver rollout plan, will run a full capacity sweep (1,2,4,8,16 concurrent) and put results into the benchmarking dashboard. will also include warmup-only and cold-start tests per region. planning to post charts later this afternoon.
priya: thanks — when you post charts, include per-host kernel_select histogram and hop counts for traces above p95. that helped a lot here. :thumbsup:
joanne: infra will also surface node labels in the console so routing rules are visible to devs.
alex: will post results: https://perf.redwood/board/edge-probe-1965432199 (timeline + kernel histos)
priya: awesome. closing the quick triage for now. if anyone sees new p95 spikes tag me.
